## 1. Overview

This report documents the data preparation pipeline for our ETF trend
prediction project, which adapts the methodology of
Sagaceta-Mejía et al. (2024) to three European ETFs:

| Ticker | Fund | Focus |
|--------|------|-------|
| **IEUR** | iShares Core MSCI Europe ETF | Broad European market |
| **FEZ** | SPDR EURO STOXX 50 ETF | Eurozone large-cap |
| **EUFN** | iShares MSCI Europe Financials ETF | European financials |
| **IVV** | iShares Core S&P 500 ETF | Developed benchmark |

Data spans **2010-01-01 → 2026-04-30**, extending the paper's original
pre-pandemic window to include recent market conditions including the
COVID-19 period and subsequent recovery.

## 4. Pipeline

```{python}
pipeline = DataPipeline(
    tickers=TICKERS,
    start=START,
    end=END,
    include_benchmark=True,
)
datasets = pipeline.run(save=True)
pipeline.summary(datasets)
```

### 4.1 Technical Indicators

The Pandas TA library (v0.4.x) expands the 6 base OHLCV features to
**~250 daily features** across 10 categories. Sparse columns with more
than 95% NaN values (e.g. ZIGZAG) are automatically removed before
cleaning.

**Look-ahead check.** Every indicator is tested for causality by
recomputing it on data truncated at day t and checking that none of
its values up to day t change. With default settings, five pandas-ta
indicators fail this test and are dropped: DPO (centred, shifts the
close backwards), the Ichimoku chikou span `ICS_26` (the close 26 days
in the future), the `TOS_STDEVALL` regression bands (fitted on the
whole sample), `VHM` (normalised with future data) and `ZIGZAG` (pivots
confirmed only by later prices). Ichimoku's forward span projections,
dated after the last trading day, are also discarded. The check runs in
the unit tests, so a library upgrade that introduces a new look-ahead
indicator fails the build.

| Category | Examples |
|----------|---------|
| Candles | Candlestick patterns |
| Cycles | Even Better SineWave (EBSW) |
| Momentum | RSI, Stochastic RSI, Williams %R, KDJ |
| Overlap | SMA, EMA, Bollinger Bands |
| Performance | Annualised returns |
| Statistics | Z-Score, variance |
| Trend | CTI, TTM Trend, ADX |
| Utility | Helper features |
| Volatility | ATR, Bollinger Band % |
| Volume | AOBV, PVR, OBV |

### 4.2 Classification Target Γ(t)

Following the paper (Section 2.4):

$$\Gamma(t) = \begin{cases} +1 & \text{if } \text{Open}(t) - \text{Open}(t-1) > 0 \\ -1 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

```{python}
fig = viz.plot_cumulative_gamma(datasets)
plt.show()
```

### 4.3 Class Balance

```{python}
fig = viz.plot_class_balance(datasets)
plt.show()
```

*All three ETFs show a slight UP bias (~51–53%), consistent across the
full 2010–2026 period including both bull and bear market phases.*

## 5. Preprocessing

### 5.1 Normalisation

Each feature is min-max scaled to **[0, 1]**, but causally: the min
and max are those observed **up to that day**, not over the whole
sample:

$$\hat{x}_t = \frac{x_t - \min_{s \le t} x_s}{\max_{s \le t} x_s - \min_{s \le t} x_s}$$

The paper scales with full-sample statistics, which leaks the future
range of every feature into earlier rows once the data is split into
walk-forward folds. Expanding-window scaling avoids this while keeping
a single processed dataset that every fold can share.

### 5.2 Cleaning

Two-stage cleaning is applied:

1. **Sparse column removal** — columns with >95% NaN (e.g. ZIGZAG
   indicator) are dropped entirely before row-level cleaning.
2. **Forward-fill** — remaining NaN values from indicator warm-up
   periods are forward-filled, then any residual NaN rows are dropped.

```{python}
for ticker, df in datasets.items():
    n_nan = df.isna().sum().sum()
    print(f"{ticker}: {len(df)} rows remaining, {n_nan} NaN values")
```

## 7. Handoff Contract

The modeling team receives:

- **Location:** `data/processed/{TICKER}_processed.parquet`
- **Schema:** DatetimeIndex + ~250 numeric feature columns + `"Gamma"` target column
- **Values:** All features scaled to [0, 1]; `Gamma` ∈ {+1, -1}; zero NaNs
- **Causality:** every feature value at day t uses only data up to day t,
  so the frame can be split into walk-forward folds as is
- **Note:** IEUR has fewer rows (~2400) than FEZ/EUFN/IVV (~3500) due
  to data availability starting June 2014

```{python}
# Verify handoff contract
for ticker, df in datasets.items():
    assert df.isna().sum().sum() == 0, f"{ticker} has NaNs!"
    assert "Gamma" in df.columns
    assert df["Gamma"].isin([1, -1]).all()
    feature_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c != "Gamma"]
    assert df[feature_cols].min().min() >= -0.01
    print(f"{ticker} ✓  shape={df.shape}")
```
